### FLOOR A — Accessibility ([`01-foundations.md`](../design-book/01-foundations.md), "The accessibility floor")

1. `--ink` and `--dim` pass **4.5:1** on any bg-ladder ground.
2. `--faint` is **never load-bearing** — provenance, ages, echoes only.
3. Anything **under 11px** is uppercase, wide-tracked, 700-weight, **and** paired with a
   non-text signal.
4. **Reduced motion is mandatory** — every motion wrapped in
   `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` or the RN equivalent. Depth may stay; travel may not.
5. **Touch targets ≥ 44px** on phone surfaces.
6. **Color never carries meaning alone** — every status color pairs with a glyph, dot,
   label, or position.

### FLOOR B — Palette and token law

7. Colors come from the surface's **token file**, not hand-rolled hex at the call site.
8. A **new** surface starts from [`tokens/starter.css`](../design-book/tokens/starter.css),
   never a copy of another app's tokens.
9. **Obsidian & Ember is the base** for a new surface; a departure is a decision with a
   record, not a default.

> Note the direction: the book states values "once, as reference with provenance — each
> app's own token file remains its runtime truth." The floor checks that the app *has* a
> token truth and uses it, not that the app's numbers match the book's.

### FLOOR C — The three laws, **bans and numbers only** ([`02-the-three-laws.md`](../design-book/02-the-three-laws.md))

**Law I · Gravity**
10. No irreversible action at tap-speed — it is **held**, with visible deepening.
11. No confirm-dialog **as a substitute** for weight.
12. No bouncy easing on consequential objects.
13. **One saturated mass per screen** — never two demands of equal visual mass.
14. **No silent soft-locks** — a state that cannot proceed says so, in words.

**Law II · The Library**
15. **Hard-delete is never the default gesture** (where it must exist, it is Law I's
    business: held, heavy, explicitly the exception).
16. **The two-move rule** — one move to invoke search, one to name the thing. Three is a
    defect.
17. **No hidden staleness** — a cached or stale value states its age.
18. **Red badges are never the only strain signal.**
19. **Nothing buried without a handle** — no unreachable content behind progressive disclosure.

**Law III · Lightning** *(the law with real numbers)*
20. Input acknowledgment **≤ 16ms** · local action **< 100ms** · anything **> 300ms shows
    its charge with a stated cost**.
21. **Nothing blocks the whole surface that doesn't own the whole surface.**
22. No entrance animation that blocks input · no spinner without stated cost · no skeleton
    that lies about layout · no alarm-styling for non-alarms.
23. **At most one thing moving at rest.** The chapter's own audit question is the test:
    *point at what's animating right now; if the answer is several things and none is a
    live process, the law is broken.*
24. Every drained, filtered, or resized surface has **one affordance returning it to
    printed value**.

**The binding doctrine**
25. **No auras, no neon, no lens flare.** Power renders as strain on the wielder.
26. **Shadows are earned, not default** ([`03-depth-and-dimension.md`](../design-book/03-depth-and-dimension.md),
    "The earned-shadow law"). **At rest, hairlines only.** A shadow appears exactly when a
    thing *lifts* — z3 held/dragged/focused, or z5 overlay — and means "currently held above
    the page." **A default drop-shadow on every card is the ban.** The z-ladder is the test,
    which is what makes this a floor item and not a taste: two readers checking whether a
    shadowed element sits at z3/z5 reach the same verdict. *(Added 2026-08-15 by Matter's
    ruling — the other half of item 25's restraint doctrine.)*

**What FILES instead of blocking** — every interpretive clause in the same chapter:
"arrives slow and settles heavy," "warm, never grim," "build for hour ten," lensing
displacement, whether a crack widens *well*, and the interplay-triangle balance. These are
real doctrine and real findings. They are not gates, because a gate keyed on taste reports
taste as defects.

### FLOOR D — Art reproducibility ([`PROCESS.md`](../ai-image-gen/PROCESS.md) §D)

Blocks the **art run's close** (P7 handoff), not a code merge.

27. **Every Tier-1 keeper carries its seed + params in its card**, mirrored at keep-time by
    `@aedl -art <plan> backfill`. Card + Seed = a regenerable recipe.
28. **Every Tier-2 (composite) keeper has its `<stem>.manifest.json` sidecar**, and the
    replay path is the one that produced it.
29. **The determinism dependencies are recorded** — checkpoint hash, the `lora-db.yml` LoRA
    hashes, the ADetailer version, clip skip.

> Why this is a floor and not a finding: an unreplayable keeper is *permanently* lost work.
> The pre-2026-07-12 composite keepers are the evidence — they cannot be reproduced, and no
> later effort can fix that.

## 6.1. What counts as design surface — the term that decides whether §6 applies

**Design surface is a property of what a diff RENDERS, never of what records a repo KEEPS.**

*Written 2026-08-17 for [mn#29](https://github.com/matterjd/matter-notes/issues/29). The phrase
was used eight times across the harness and defined in none of them, which left the axis's
behaviour on any diff without obvious UI resting on the reader.*

**Where it comes from — it is derived, not invented.** Every one of §6's checks measures a
**rendered artifact**: a contrast ratio, a type size, a touch target, a token source, an easing
curve, a latency budget, a shadow's z-level, a keeper's seed. So the scope follows from the floor
itself — **a diff has design surface exactly when it changes something at least one floor item can
be measured against.** Anything else is a design *record*, and records are the Spec axis's business.

### The test — a positive enumeration

A diff has design surface **if and only if** it changes at least one of:

1. **Rendered UI** — components, templates, screens: the files that emit what a person sees
   (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.html`, RN screens, Angular templates).
2. **Style, token, or theme definitions** — CSS/SCSS, style objects, token files, theme configs,
   and any hand-rolled colour at a **rendering** call site (a hex literal used as a grep needle
   in a build script is an instrument, not a declaration — both judges hit this).
3. **Motion and timing a person perceives** — transitions, easing, durations,
   `prefers-reduced-motion` handling, spinners, skeletons.
4. **Interaction affordances** — press/gesture handlers, hold-to-confirm flows, focus and keyboard
   behaviour, hit-target sizing, disclosure and navigation structure.
5. **Generated image artifacts and their provenance** — keepers, cards, seeds,
   `<stem>.manifest.json` sidecars (FLOOR D).

**Explicitly NOT design surface** — the common cases, named so that no judge has to infer them:

- Build tooling, CI workflows, shell scripts, package manifests, lockfiles, version bumps.
- Docs, prose, markdown, charters, ADRs, run records — **including `docs/design/` itself**.
- Tests, fixtures, types, and pure logic or data modules with no rendered output.
- Terminal / CLI output (see the carve-out below).

> **Answered outright, because it is the common case: a diff touching only build tooling, CI,
> scripts and docs has NO design surface.** The axis still runs and returns
> `no design surface in this diff`. That return is the finding — not a skip, and not a pass.

### Two tiebreakers, because lists alone do not decide

*Added 2026-08-17 from the two-judge repeatability control (mn#29). Both judges returned the same
verdict on the dry-run target — and both, independently, reported the same structural gap: the
inclusion list above is **content**-typed while the exclusion list is **file**-typed, so one file
can satisfy both.*

**1. The exclusions are defeasible, and the test runs on HUNKS, not filenames.** If a hunk inside
an otherwise-excluded file changes a clause 1–5 property, **that hunk carries design surface**.
Three live examples, all in the dry-run range and all resolved by luck rather than by rule:

- `apps/desktop/angular.json` is build tooling **and** holds the `styles[]` array (`:32`, `:112`).
  The range's actual change was `"statsJson": true`, not a style property — so the null held. A
  diff swapping that `styles[]` entry would file-type as excluded and return a **false null**.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` is a package manifest **and** carries the window's
  rendered geometry (`width: 1440`, `height: 900`, `:17-18`). The range's change was a version
  string.
- A version string is excluded as a "version bump" — but one that ships into an About or status
  surface is a rendered artifact, and the hunk rule is what catches it.

**Path exclusions still defeat extension inclusions.** `docs/design/phase1-dashboard/` holds 14
genuinely rendered `.html` files and a `foundations/tokens.html`; clause 1 lists `.html` and clause
2 lists "token files". The exclusion wins — they are the repo's design **records**. Stated out loud
so that two readers are not left reconciling two lists.

**2. Measuring a rendered property is not changing it.** A diff that only **gates, budgets, or
witnesses** a rendered property does not thereby have design surface — the surface belongs to the
diff that *moves the number*. The dry-run range is the worked example, and both judges named it as
the sharpest edge: its entire subject is a witness over initial-chunk size, which is upstream of
item 20's latency budgets, and it still returns no design surface.

> **If you re-run the terminal measurement above, read this first.** A colour probe containing bare
> `tput` or `ansi` returns dozens of false hits in `scripts/deferred-field-gate.sh` alone — `tput`
> matches inside "ou*tput*", `ansi` inside "tr*ansi*tively". **Three readers hit this in one
> session**: the author of this section and both judges. A self-check against `echo "hello"` does
> **not** catch it — the plain control must itself contain the words *output* and *transitively*,
> or it certifies a broken instrument. Use `\btput\b` and raw `\x1b`. Measured at `0f0e280`.

### The trap this closes

**A design *record* is not design *surface*.** The Design Reviewer brief orders the judge to read
the repo's own design records **first** — and `docs/design/` is a records directory. Reading it is
how the judge learns the repo's precedence; it is never evidence that the diff has surface.

The concrete failure, from the 2026-08-15 dry run's own target: `command-center` carries
`docs/design/213-initial-chunk-witness.md`, a falsifiable **engineering** design for that exact
slice with a numbered §7 decision list. A judge reading *has-a-design-record* as
*has-design-surface* does not return the null — it reviews the build against those decisions and
reports drift. **Those findings would be real and misfiled**: checking an implementation against
its design doc is the **Spec** axis's job, and §5's *"do not merge or rerank across axes"* means a
misfiled finding cannot be moved afterwards. Ambiguity here does not produce a wrong finding; it
produces a correct finding in the wrong axis, which is harder to spot and harder to triage.

### Prose

Prose **rendered in a surface a person operates** is design surface — items 14 and 17 measure
exactly that (a state that cannot proceed *says so, in words*; a stale value *states its age*).
Prose **in the repo's documents** is not. The test is where it ships: to a screen, or to a reader
of the repo.

### Terminal / CLI output — not design surface by default

The reason is mechanical, not doctrinal, and it is **the same ground on which ubiquitous language
was excluded from the floor** (§6's grown-once note). Most of the floor's items cannot be evaluated
against a terminal at all: contrast belongs to the user's theme rather than the app's, and there is
no token file, no touch target, and no z-ladder. Two or three items (6, 20, 22) plausibly reach it —
and a floor that fires on three of twenty-nine either reports noise or gets quietly skipped, and a
skipped floor item teaches every reader that floor items are optional.

**Where a repo carries a CLI style guide, terminal output is available as a declared added axis**
(`aedl-verify` §4's added-axes rule) — exactly the route ubiquitous language took. Declare it at
spawn time with its own question; do not smuggle it into the floor.

> **Measured on the dry-run target, 2026-08-17.** `deferred-field-gate.sh`, `qa-gate.sh` and
> `session-open-ritual.sh` carry **zero** terminal colour — no ESC bytes, no `tput`, no literal
> `\033`/`\e[` — on an instrument self-checked against a coloured probe and a plain one first.
> So this carve-out does not change that run's verdict; it removes the coin-flip from the next one.

### Governance

This defines the **scope** of the existing floor. It adds, removes, and rewords **no floor item**,
so it does not need Matter's §9 y/n. If he would rather it sat under §9 anyway, say so and it moves.
